name: Hepher
overview: Hepher was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Ashhur and Naarah. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his lineage, with no additional notes or significant narrative details recorded. This positions Hepher primarily as a genealogical figure within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Hepher is a proper name that possibly means 'help,' though this is not definitively stated. The name was not given directly by God but appears in the genealogical record in 1 Chronicles 4:6. No titles or additional names are associated with Hepher.
familyAndRelationships: Hepher is explicitly recorded as the son of Ashhur and Naarah, establishing his immediate family within the tribe of Judah. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these parents for Hepher.
scriptureSignificance: Hepher's significance lies in his role as a descendant within the tribe of Judah, contributing to the genealogical record that traces God's chosen people. While he does not have a prominent narrative or direct theological role, his inclusion affirms the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of Judah, from which the Messiah would ultimately come. His presence in the biblical record underscores the importance of family lines in God's redemptive plan.
